# `Scanner/NoiseSNR-v0` · Measure the signal-to-noise ratio of a protocol

**C · The system** · RF chain · kind 1, measure · isolates C12: Receiver noise: its level and its dependence on bandwidth. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** ADMITTED: on 300 fresh instances per level the reference passes >= 99 %, no policy that ignores the object passes more than 3 % (95 % bounds)

One test of acceptance and quality control, on its own. The signal is read off the image; the noise is not: the pixel scatter inside a region holds the coil shading, and the background of a magnitude image is Rayleigh distributed and carries ghosts. The standards answer with two acquisitions and their difference image (noise = SD of the difference / sqrt(2)) or with a background region and the factor 0.655. At level 3 the phantom fills the field of view and a ghost covers the background, so of these two only the first is left.

Kind of task: **measurement** (the reference is a fixed scan list (the protocol twice) with a fixed estimator; `open_loop` plays it: no scan depends on an earlier one).

```python
import mrgym
env = mrgym.make("Scanner/NoiseSNR-v0", level=2, seed=0)
obs, info = env.reset()
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A uniform phantom in a scanner with a hidden receiver noise level and a hidden receive-coil shading; a stated spin-echo protocol; three marked regions; scan time for the protocol two or three times | For each marked region, the signal-to-noise ratio of the stated protocol | A noise-free scan of the stated protocol on the hidden system and the true noise standard deviation of a pixel of that protocol: every delivered ratio must agree with signal / noise |

## World

- On the table: ACR-type phantom, uniform section (world kind acr, slice 7), 1.5 T or 3 T
- Sequences that matter here: se
- Formulas the agent is given: noise = SD(image 1 - image 2) / sqrt(2); background of a magnitude image: SD = 0.655 x noise, mean = 1.253 x noise; SNR = mean signal / noise (level 1 states the first)

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| receiver noise density (the SNR of the middle region lies between 60 and 600) | the phantom |
| the receive sensitivity, which falls across the phantom in a hidden direction | the protocol and its scan time |
| transmit gain | the three regions |
| level 3: the pulse-to-pulse instability that puts a ghost over the background | the definition of the SNR and the tolerance |
| the 128-bit world seed | level 1: the two-acquisition procedure |
|  | the instrument datasheet |
|  | realised protocol, timing and cost of every plan and scan |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'snr': {'<region id>': '<plain ratio>'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan
- Error: `largest over the regions of |delivered / (noise-free signal / true noise SD) - 1|`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates and, for every region, error <= 10 %

## What the agent reads at reset (level 2, seed 0)

~~~text
# Measure the signal-to-noise ratio of a protocol
A test phantom lies at the isocentre of a 3 T scanner: a disc of solution, 190 mm inner
diameter, one material. The examination needs the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) that this protocol gives in each
marked region:
    sequence se, tr_ms 600, te_ms 20, fov_mm 250, matrix 256, slice_mm 5,
    bandwidth_hz_per_px 130, averages 1, pe_dir y   (one scan: 157.2 s)
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre; each lies inside the phantom):
  R1: y 51.5, x 19.4, radius 18
  R2: y -8.9, x -54.3, radius 18
  R3: y -42.5, x 34.9, radius 18
SNR of a region: its mean signal in the magnitude image of this protocol, divided by the standard deviation of the
noise in one pixel of that image.
Deliver one SNR per region (R1, R2, R3) with `submit`. Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names.
Every scan you run is charged to the scan-time budget, a scan of this protocol too.
Nothing about the receiver, the coil or the state of the system is known in advance.

Passing: for every region, the delivered SNR is within 10 % of the scanner's own value: the mean signal of the
region in a noise-free scan of the protocol, divided by the true noise standard deviation of a pixel of that protocol.
The scanner's log must show that you measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong (a plain ratio, not decibels).
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's scan is noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
